meta.note: Primary items quote the Supreme Court's own record of proceedings or judgment, or a High Court order. Press items quote the report as fetched on 2026-10-09; the court's order was not found.

items.case: Mahua Moitra v. Election Commission of India (writ petition, Supreme Court)
items.headline: Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra moves Supreme Court against electoral roll revision in Bihar
items.claim: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra asked the Supreme Court to quash the Commission's order of 24 June 2025 and to stop it from ordering the same revision in other states, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: a direction to quash the Order dated 24.06.2025 issued by Election Commission of India ... restraining Election Commission of India from issuing similar orders for Special Intensive Revision

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, Diary No. 35785 of 2025, with six other petitions
items.headline: Petitions against the Bihar revision listed for 10 July
items.claim: Counsel for ADR and other petitioners mentioned seven petitions against the Bihar revision, and the Court let them be filed during the vacation and listed them for 10 July 2025.
items.quote: Leave to file the petition(s) during Partial Court Working Days is granted, with an advance copy of the petition(s) to be given to the appropriate authorities. List the petitions on 10.07.2025 [Thursday].

items.outlet: Supreme Court of India (judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564, para 10.8)
items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: Notice issued, and three questions framed
items.claim: The Court issued notice to the Commission and said the petitions raised three questions about its power, its method and the timing before the Bihar election, according to the account in the Court's 2026 judgment.
items.quote: Upon hearing the parties on 10.07.2025, this Court, while issuing notice to the Commission, observed that on a prima facie appraisal, three substantial questions arise for determination: first, the very authority of the Commission to embark upon the impugned exercise; second, the procedure and methodology adopted in carrying out the exercise, including the method prescribed by the Commission to ascertain the Citizenship of the Voters; and third, the propriety of its timing

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: The list of 65 lakh names to be published with reasons
items.claim: The Court recorded the Commission's agreement to publish, district by district and searchable by EPIC number, the list of about 65 lakh electors left off the Bihar draft roll with the reason for each.
items.quote: The list of 65,00,000 (approximate) voters, whose names appeared in the Voter List as on 2025 but are not included in the Draft Roll dated 01.08.2025, shall be displayed on the websites of the District Election Officers (District-wise).

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: Aadhaar to be accepted as the 12th document
items.claim: The Court directed the Commission to accept Aadhaar as proof of identity for the Bihar revision and said it is no proof of citizenship.
items.quote: Accordingly, we direct the Election Commission of India and its authorities to accept Aadhar Card as a proof of identity for the purpose of inclusion or exclusion in the revised voter list of the State of Bihar. Aadhaar Card, for this purpose, shall be treated as the 12th document by the Authorities.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 855 of 2025, tagged with Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: A petition in support of the revision
items.claim: The Court issued notice on 8 September 2025 on W.P.(C) 855 of 2025, which its 2026 judgment describes as a petition asking for such revisions to be held at regular intervals.
items.quote: We deem it appropriate to clarify that certain petitions (for instance, Writ Petition (Civil) No. 855 of 2025) have in fact been instituted in support of the SIR exercise. The Petitioner(s) in these cases have urged that such an exercise ought to be conducted at regular intervals to prevent and curb the inclusion of ineligible persons in the electoral rolls on account of illegal influx.

items.case: B Sathyanarayanan v. The Chief Election Commissioner and Another, W.P. No. 39744 of 2025, Madras High Court
items.headline: SIR of Tamil Nadu electoral rolls will begin in a week, Election Commission tells Madras High Court
items.claim: A former AIADMK MLA asked the Madras High Court to order a re-verification of 229 booths in T. Nagar, and the Court adjourned the case after the Commission said the revision would begin within a week, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: The court took note of the submissions and adjourned the case by a week.

items.case: Public interest litigation on the SIR in West Bengal, Calcutta High Court
items.headline: Calcutta High Court asks EC to submit affidavit on PIL challenging SIR in West Bengal
items.claim: A PIL asked the Calcutta High Court to have the West Bengal revision use the current roll in place of the 2002 roll and to protect booth level officers, and the Court asked the Commission for an affidavit, The Week reported.
items.quote: The court ordered ECI to file a short affidavit within 10 days on November 18 on the need for the SIR in West Bengal.

items.case: Petitions of the DMK, CPI(M), West Bengal Congress and Trinamool Congress leaders against the order of 27 October 2025, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court seeks ECI's response on pleas challenging SIR in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal
items.claim: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the second phase in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal and asked the High Courts to hold back their own cases on the revision, The Leaflet reported.
items.quote: we request the jurisdictional High Courts to keep in abeyance or defer the writ proceedings

items.case: State of Kerala v. Election Commission of India, 2025 SCC OnLine Ker 12336, Kerala High Court
items.headline: Kerala HC refuses to entertain State's plea to defer SIR leaving it open to approach Supreme Court
items.claim: The Kerala government asked the High Court to put off the revision until the local body elections ended, and the Court dismissed the petition because the Supreme Court had asked High Courts to hold back such cases, SCC Online reported.
items.quote: judicial discipline and comity also require the Court to refrain from entertaining the writ petition

items.case: Petition of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on booth level officers, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court issues directions to ease BLO workload in SIR exercise
items.claim: On a TVK petition saying 35 to 40 booth level officers had died under work pressure, the Court told states to provide more staff and cut working hours, National Herald reported.
items.quote: governments cannot remain indifferent when BLOs are pushed to the brink

items.case: State of Kerala and political party leaders v. Election Commission of India, Supreme Court

items.claim: The Kerala government and leaders of the IUML, Congress and CPI(M) asked for more time for enumeration forms, and the Court put off a decision to 18 December, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: will take a call then on whether to pass further extension

items.case: PIL No. 1272 of 2025, Allahabad High Court
items.headline: Allahabad High Court rejects PIL to adopt ECI's SIR guidelines for UP three-tier panchayat roll revision
items.claim: A PIL asked the Allahabad High Court to apply the Commission's revision guidelines to Uttar Pradesh's panchayat rolls, and the Court dismissed it, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: there is absolutely no reason for this Court to interfere

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)

items.quote: The names of the persons figuring in the logical discrepancies may be displayed at the Gram Panchayat Bhawans, public places in every Taluka and Block Office of every Taluka (Sub-Division), as well as in the Ward Offices in the cities of the urban areas.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
items.headline: Appeals to tribunals of former judges
items.claim: The Court recorded that over 10,16,000 objections had been decided by judicial officers and directed that appeals go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges.
items.quote: our order dated 24.02.2026, in no uncertain terms, points out that the orders passed by the judicial officers will not be subjected to appeal before any Executive/Administrative Officer.

items.case: Suo Motu W.P.(C) No. 3 of 2026, In Re: Safety and Security of Judicial Officers Deputed for Work Relating to SIR of Electoral Rolls in the State of West Bengal
items.headline: Court acts after judicial officers are surrounded in Maldah
items.claim: After seven judicial officers deciding SIR claims were held at a BDO office in Maldah, the Court ordered central forces for them and asked the Commission to give the inquiry to the CBI or the NIA.
items.quote: The ECI is directed for requisitioning of adequate central forces and for their deployment at all places where the judicial officers have been deputed for adjudication of objections under the SIR process.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal), with W.P.(C) No. 462 of 2026
items.headline: A pending appeal gives no vote
items.claim: On petitions from people deleted after the judicial officers' check, the Court directed that appeals decided before polling go into a supplementary roll and said a pending appeal gave no right to vote.
items.quote: However, it goes without saying that the mere pendency of appeals preferred by excluded persons before the Appellate Tribunals shall not entitle them to exercise their right to vote.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
items.headline: West Bengal SIR: SC pushes SIR disputes to Calcutta HC as appeal backlog mounts
items.claim: Counsel told the Court that 136 of nearly 27 lakh appeals had been decided, and the Court declined fresh grievances and sent the parties to the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, Supreme Court Observer reported.
items.quote: Please approach the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: The Supreme Court upholds the Bihar revision
items.claim: The Court held the Bihar revision lawful under section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324 and said declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen.
items.quote: It does not amount to a declaration that the individual is not a citizen of India; it merely reflects the Commission’s inability to be satisfied, for electoral purposes, that the statutory conditions are met.

items.outlet: Supreme Court of India (2026 INSC 564, para 186(h))
items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: Citizenship cases to the competent authority, and judicial review for wrong deletions
items.claim: The Court directed the Commission to refer within four weeks the cases it deleted as non-citizens to the authority under the Citizenship Act and allowed people in Bihar whose names were, in the Court's words, "erroneously deleted" as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate to seek judicial review.
items.quote: Regarding persons whose names have been deleted from the 2003 roll on account of the Commission being of the opinion that they are not citizens, the Commission shall refer such cases within 4 weeks to the Competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955, for adjudication of their citizenship.

items.outlet: High Court for the State of Telangana (order reproduced by LiveLaw)
items.case: Writ Petition No. 20188 of 2026
items.headline: Deleted voter told to use the SIR
items.claim: A Charminar voter asked the High Court to restore his family's deleted names, and the Court dismissed the petition and told him to use the revision then under way.
items.quote: Therefore, the petitioner is at liberty to participate in the process of SIR in respect of his grievances relating to deletion of his name and the names of his family members from the electoral rolls earlier. This court, therefore, is not inclined to interfere in the instant writ petition.

items.case: Writ petition by Adivasi Sena, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana HC seeks response on plea against non-tribal voters in Scheduled Areas
items.claim: Adivasi Sena asked the Telangana High Court to have ineligible non-tribal voters deleted from the rolls of the Fifth Schedule Areas during the revision, and the Court sought replies, Telangana Today reported.
items.quote: directed the respondents to file their counters within two weeks

items.case: Batch of writ petitions on G.O.Ms. No. 172, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana HC takes up plea on Family Register Certificate as voter eligibility proof
items.claim: Petitioners asked the Telangana High Court to strike the state's Family Register Certificate from the revision's list of documents, and the Court gave the Commission time and listed the case for 12 August, Telangana Today reported.
items.quote: cannot be treated as a valid eligibility document for voter enrollment under the Special Intensive Revision

items.case: PIL on homeless and demolition-displaced voters, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: plea to include homeless and demolition-displaced voters
items.claim: A PIL asked the Delhi High Court for special arrangements so homeless and displaced people could enrol in the revision, and the Court reserved its order and said it would not monitor the policy, LiveLaw reported. LiveLaw reported on 1 September that the bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia had dismissed the petition. The Court said the Commission's Manual on Electoral Rolls already provides, in clause 8.5, how a homeless person's ordinary residence is determined, so the fear that homeless people would be left off the draft appeared to be without basis. It said any elector left off the roll after a demolition or relocation can file Form 6.
items.quote: everything cannot be thrust upon courts
items.response: The Court said the petition gave no particulars or numbers of people displaced by demolitions who remained off the roll. The Commission told the Court that clause 8.5 lets homeless people enrol without documentary proof of residence once a booth level officer has checked over more than one night that they sleep at the address given, Bar and Bench reported.
items.note: Dismissal: LiveLaw, by Malavika Prasad, published 1 September 2026, 4:05 pm IST, 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 797, W.P.(C) 11942/2026, https://www.livelaw.in/high-court/delhi-high-court/delhi-high-court-rejects-pil-include-homeless-demolition-displaced-persons-sir-548104 ; Bar and Bench, by Prashant Jha, published 1 September 2026, 9:57 am IST. Both read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. Neither gives the date of the order. The petitioner, named in the case title, is a private person and is not named.

items.case: Writ petition by a deleted elector working abroad, Calcutta High Court
items.headline: Calcutta High Court directs SIR tribunal to expeditiously decide plea of Saudi resident unable to renew passport over voter list deletion
items.claim: A man deleted in the revision said it was blocking his passport renewal, and the Calcutta High Court told the appellate tribunal to decide his appeal within two weeks without going into the merits, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: directed the concerned SIR Appellate Tribunal to dispose of the pending appeal within two weeks

items.case: Devender Yadav & Anr v. Election Commission of India & Anr, 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 835, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: High Court refuses to entertain plea against first-time applicant declaration for deleted voters, says file PIL
items.claim: Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav challenged the Form 6 declaration that voters left off the draft must sign as first-time applicants, and he withdrew the petition after the Court told him to file it as a PIL, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: The plea was accordingly withdrawn.

items.case: Petition of two transparency activists under Article 32, Supreme Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: SC says notices going to people mechanically, asks EC to adopt additional safeguards
items.claim: Two transparency activists who had petitioned the Court asked for the list of Delhi voters sent notices and the criteria for logical discrepancies, and the bench told the Commission to look at extra safeguards, ThePrint reported.
items.quote: The notices are going to people almost mechanically. Just look whether some additional safeguards are needed.

items.case: W.P.(Crl.) No. 401 of 2026, against decisions of the Chief Election Commissioner, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court says modified Form 6 not approved by it
items.claim: A petition asked the Court to quash 14 decisions it said the Chief Election Commissioner took alone, and the Court issued notice, tagged it with a similar case and said it had not approved any modified Form 6, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'No Business Asking Them to Fill Form 6 Because System Didn't Allow Form 8': Bombay HC Condemns ECI's Handling of SIR Process
items.claim: A family of six who moved house within the same constituency filed Form 8 and were then deleted from the roll, because the ERONET software found no record of their cards and allowed only a rejection. The bench asked the Commission to show where the law allows a deletion without a hearing and said the family should not have been asked to file Form 6, The Wire reported, citing The Times of India.
items.quote: Questioning the legality of the removal of the Santa Cruz family from the voter list without a hearing, the bench noted, "Show us from the Act where it empowers you to delete without hearing. If you are planning to remove someone's name, you have to give the person an opportunity of hearing first." ... According to TOI, the bench replied, "You have no business asking them to fill Form 6 because the system didn't allow you to do it on Form 8. That was the problem."
items.response: The Wire reported that the Commission's counsel said other voters deleted in the same way had been put back on the roll after filing Form 6, and that the family had not filed Form 6 when asked to.
items.note: PTI via Telangana Today (1 Oct 2026, 11:18 AM) agrees on the hearing date (Wednesday 30 Sept), the bench, the six family members in Santa Cruz, Form 8, ERONET offering only 'reject', and the bench's 'Show us from the Act...what empowers you to delete without hearing?'. It adds that the court said the draft roll cannot be the basis for deletion. It does not carry the 'no business' line, which The Wire attributes to TOI. Both sources name the petitioner; the draft does not.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'What Is SIR's Purpose If Citizens Are Being Removed From Voter's List? Bombay High Court Asks ECI
items.claim: At a further hearing of the same family's petition the bench asked what purpose the revision served if citizens were left off the roll. It also asked why a voter who had moved house should have to sign the enumeration form, whose declaration says the voter still lives at the address on the existing roll, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: "Read the judgment, it says ECI has an obligation to ensure that all Indian citizens are on the list... If citizens are excluded what will we do with your SIR? If citizens are being removed from the list then what is the purpose of this entire SIR process then?" ... "If a voter comes to you with Form 8, saying he has changed his address you just cannot tell that person that look your name isn't included in the draft roll now you will have to fill in Form 6 (inclusion of new voter). Your enumeration form, basically has a declaration that a person continues to live in the address as mentioned in the existing voters list. But consider, if someone has changed their residence, can you compel the person to make a false declaration by submitting that pre-filled enumeration? Why can't that person simply give a Form 8 because anyway, his name is there in the existing list he just wants to get his address changed.. Why compel enumeration form?" Justice Menezes observed.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that the Commission's counsel argued that a voter had to submit the enumeration form along with Form 8 to have an address changed, and that a voter who did not submit it had to file Form 6.

items.case: Petition on the implementation of the SIR in Maharashtra, Bombay High Court
items.headline: Maharashtra SIR: Bombay High Court Declines Oral Plea To Restrain ECI From Deleting Voters' Names, Says SC Seized Of Issue
items.claim: The Chief Justice's bench refused an oral request to order that no names be deleted from the roll in Maharashtra for the time being. It said it would follow the Supreme Court, which it was told had restrained High Courts in November 2025 from hearing petitions on the revision, and adjourned the case by four weeks, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for the order and reasons behind the revision in the state and for safeguards against wrongful exclusion.
items.quote: "There are restraining orders already... No purpose will be served by a parallel litigation. Let the SC hear the matter first and we will consider it later," Chief Justice said. ... The judges turned down the said oral prayer, by observing, "No no no...we are not going to pass any such orders... We will follow judicial propriety." The bench accordingly, adjourned the hearing for four weeks.
items.note: LiveLaw gives no case number. The petition alleges BLOs in Maharashtra asked for supporting documents with enumeration forms; that is the petitioners' allegation and is left out of the claim.

items.case: MA Baby v. Union of India and others, WP(c) 63560/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Don't Completely Stop Trains/Metro In Delhi To Handle October 10 Protests : Supreme Court To Centre
items.claim: The Supreme Court told the Centre not to stop all trains and Metro services in Delhi before the 10 October protests against the Chief Election Commissioner, and to run them in a regulated way, LiveLaw reported. The petition was brought by CPI(M) General Secretary MA Baby and others against the closure of 57 Metro stations and the cancellation of trains due at New Delhi and Nizamuddin. The order said the notifications appeared to be overreaching, and ETV Bharat reported that the bench also asked the Centre to reconsider Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site.
items.quote: there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of Metro trains
items.response: The order records that the Solicitor General "has fairly agreed to impress upon the authorities to reassess such prohibitions." He said the impression that the whole city had been shut "is far from the truth."
items.note: One item for two reports of the same order: LiveLaw (553920, with the case number) and ETV Bharat. ETV Bharat prints the order's sentence as "We make it clear that there shall not be complete prohibition on movement of Metro/trains"; LiveLaw's wording is used here. The 57 stations are the Court's figure and the train times Kapil Sibal's statement, per LiveLaw 553880. The protest was called by the Cockroach Janta Party and opposition parties.

items.case: Contempt petition against the Union Home Secretary, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the DMRC chairperson, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court Contempt Plea Alleges Delhi Authorities Defied Order On Metro, Train Curbs
items.claim: A contempt plea filed in the Supreme Court on 10 October alleged that the Centre and Delhi authorities defied the Court's order of 9 October, keeping 57 Metro stations shut and cancelling Delhi-bound trains before the protest against the Chief Election Commissioner, Outlook reported. The plea also said no traffic advisory had been published in newspapers. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana listed it to be heard with a petition against the detention of opposition leaders at a special sitting on Sunday 11 October, Bar and Bench reported. On 15 October, before the Chief Justice and Justice Bagchi, the Delhi Police Commissioner filed two affidavits that tendered an unconditional apology for any perceived non-compliance and said there had been no non-compliance with the Court's orders of 9 and 11 October. Justice Bagchi observed that on the Solicitor General's account the apology appeared qualified.
items.quote: "Notwithstanding the solemn judicial mandate and the assurance recorded before the bench of the Chief Justice of India (CJI), the contemnors have consciously maintained a blanket shutdown across transit corridors, persisted with unwarranted train cancellations, and failed to issue or publicize transparent traffic and transit advisories."
items.response: The Solicitor General said the apology was included as standard practice in answering a contempt notice and that the government was defending its actions on facts. The Commissioner asked for the contempt notice to be discharged.
items.note: Outlook and Hindustan Times name different advocates as the filer; the filer is left out. The plea is the petitioner's allegation. The special sitting is from Bar and Bench, by Debayan Roy, 10 October 2026, 8:09 pm IST (https://www.barandbench.com/news/delhi-protests-supreme-court-to-hold-special-sunday-sitting-to-hear-pleas-against-detention-of-opposition-leaders), which also names the filer and the three officials; the filer stays out. The affidavits and the exchange of 15 October are from Bar and Bench, by Ritwik Choudhury, 15 October 2026, 6:30 pm IST (modified 17 October). Both read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The quoted words of the affidavits are 'unconditional and unqualified apology' and 'no non-compliance much less any wilful or deliberate non-compliance'.

items.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
items.headline: SIR-Deleted Voters Move Supreme Court For Expeditious Disposal Of Appeals Before Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections
items.claim: Five electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication applied to the Supreme Court for their appeals to be decided before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections, LiveLaw reported. They also asked for a Special Investigation Team to examine how the revision's decisions were made. The application cites the Commission's affidavits as showing 1.7 lakh appeals pending from Kolkata and Howrah.
items.quote: The applicants claim that their names were deleted without any notice to them.
items.response: None was reported. The applicants say the Chief Electoral Officer has not published the criteria for logical discrepancies.
items.note: Filing date not given; the date is the publication date. Applicants are private persons and are not named.

items.case: Application by five deleted electors in the West Bengal SIR matter, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'We Are Conscious' : Supreme Court To Consider Plea To Prioritise SIR-Deleted Voters' Appeals Ahead Of Kolkata, Howrah Municipal Elections
items.claim: Counsel for electors deleted from West Bengal's roll after adjudication asked the Supreme Court to hear their plea before the Kolkata and Howrah municipal elections and to let appellants vote, LiveLaw reported. The Chief Justice said the Court would try to list it on 16 October, or else on 29 October, and suggested the tribunals take up appeals for inclusion first and appeals seeking deletion last. Counsel told the Court that nearly 1.70 lakh appeals from the two municipal areas were pending.
items.quote: We will find out if we can list on 16th (Friday) ...otherwise 29th is best way.
items.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. The figures put to the Court were counsel's, partly drawn from the Commission's affidavits.
items.note: Mentioned on Friday 9 October before CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. UNI confirms the 16 October listing. Counsel said the main West Bengal SIR matter had been put back to 30 October.

items.case: Paka Suresh v. Union of India, SLP(C) No. 35786/2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Andhra Pradesh Local Body Elections | Conduct Polls As Per Old Rolls If SIR Not Complete Before Notification: Supreme Court
items.claim: The Supreme Court said Andhra Pradesh's local body elections should use the revised roll if it is published before the elections are notified, and the existing roll if it is not. It said the revision cannot be a reason to delay the polls.
items.quote: the elections would be conducted using the existing electoral rolls in accordance with the applicable State laws.
items.response: The Election Commission proposed publishing the final SIR roll on 16 October 2026. The State Election Commission said the rolls in force continue until the Commission publishes a fresh list. Deccan Chronicle reported on 15 October that the Commission had moved the final publication in Andhra Pradesh to 30 October and the last date for disposing of claims and objections to 22 October. The Wire reported that nominations for the state's urban local body elections were being filed when the YSRCP moved the Supreme Court on 20 October over violence during their filing.
items.note: Bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, Friday 9 October. The petitioner's counsel's figure of about 44 lakh voters removed is a party's submission and is left out. Deccan Chronicle (DC Correspondent), published 15 October 2026, 12:35 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The Wire (The Wire Staff), 'Free and Fair Election is a Basic Structure of Constitution...', published 22 October 2026, 6:14 pm IST, read in full through The Wire's CMS API on 24 October 2026, https://thewire.in/law/free-and-fair-election-is-a-basic-structure-of-constitution-supreme-court . No source read says which roll the local body polls use.

items.case: WP 32975 of 2026, a petition by two electors, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana SIR (full headline not captured; search listing title)
items.claim: The Telangana High Court asked the Commission why one petitioner was left off the roll without a notice and what happened to the other after his hearing, LiveLaw reported. The petition challenges notices over minor discrepancies and the automated matching used in the revision. The case was listed again for 13 October. At the hearing of 13 October, senior counsel for the Commission said one petitioner's name had been deleted and he would have to file Form 6, and that the other's petition was premature because the final roll had not been published, Telangana Today reported. He assured the bench that reasoned orders, open to appeal, would be passed where electors on the draft were left off the final roll, provided they attended the hearings on their notices and gave documents. He said that where no order was passed, the elector's name could be taken as included. The case was adjourned to 15 October.
items.quote: If he has satisfied and explained on the mismatch, you must have taken a decision on that,
items.response: The Commission's counsel sought time for instructions. She said the second petitioner was sent a notice over a mismatch in his father's name and heard on 15 September, and that the first could file Form 6.
items.note: Bench of Justice P Sam Koshy and Justice Narsing Rao Nandikonda. Petitioners named in the case title are private persons and are not named. Hearing of Tuesday 13 October: Telangana Today (no byline), published 13 October 2026, 11:27 pm IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. It gives the bench as Acting Chief Justice P. Sam Koshy and Justice Nandikonda Narsing Rao, senior counsel L. Ravi Chander for the petitioners and senior counsel Avinash Desai for the Commission. The report names the petitioners, who are private persons and are not named here. No report of the hearing of 15 October was read.

items.case: Writ petition by a family of St Cruz constituency
items.headline: Goa HC adjourns hearing on plea challenging voter deletion as ECI points out SC cases
items.claim: The Bombay High Court at Goa adjourned a family's petition against the deletion of their names in Goa's revision after the Commission said the Supreme Court's pending cases could bear on it.
items.quote: The orders the Supreme Court may pass can have a bearing on the matter before the HC,
items.response: The Commission's counsel also said "what is under challenge is the rejection of Form 8" and that it "cannot be looked at in isolation."
items.note: Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar. Adjourned to the following Tuesday, 13 October. The family is not named.

items.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
items.headline: SC registry points out 10 defects in Rahul Gandhi's plea in SIR case
items.claim: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and other INDIA bloc leaders filed a writ petition in the Supreme Court on 12 October against the Election Commission, the Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners. Delhi Police had stopped their march to the Court on Bhagwant Das Road earlier that day, and counsel filed the petition shortly before the filing counter closed. The petition asks for the SIR to be suspended in every state while the case is heard, for a committee under a retired Supreme Court judge to audit the names left off or deleted, and for the Commission's files on its decision to hold the revision. PTI reported that the Registry flagged more than ten defects in it, among them illegible or missing pages, an unclear copy of Kharge's identity card and a court fee short by over Rs 200. LawBeat reported that the Registry registered it on 13 October once the defects were cured.
items.quote: Besides, the registry also pointed out a shortfall of over Rs 200 in court fee.
items.response: No response from the Commission was reported.
items.note: PTI (New Delhi, 12 Oct, 11:47 pm IST, defects attributed to 'sources') says more than 10 defects and itemises three. The Week (13 Oct) says 'at least 14' in its body and 'over 10' in its headline, and lists eight, including the naming of the CEC and the two ECs as respondents and a missing similarity paragraph. Other outlets give Rs 220 for the fee shortfall. Case number and diary number from LiveLaw 554801 and LawBeat 1642122; the registration on 13 October is LawBeat's. The Week (12 Oct, 5:49 pm) gives the march route, the stop on Bhagwant Das Road and the filing through the AoR before the counter closed. The prayers are from LiveLaw 554801 and The Week of 13 October. The petition's own count of names removed is the petitioners' figure and is left out. Removal of the CEC is not among the prayers LiveLaw lists. LiveLaw names ten petitioners at filing and two who joined later.

items.case: Rahul Gandhi v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 1351 of 2026 (Diary No. 64196 of 2026), Supreme Court
items.headline: 'One Petitioner Has To Explain His Conduct': Supreme Court Issues Notice On INDIA Bloc Leaders' Petition Against ECI Over SIR
items.claim: A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on the INDIA bloc leaders' petition to the Election Commission, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and tagged it with the SIR cases already pending, LiveLaw reported. The Chief Justice said that issuing notice did not mean the Court was condemning anything. He said the Court would ask one of the petitioners about his conduct, and Bar and Bench reported that notice on that petitioner's behalf was entertained provisionally until he explained it at the next hearing. The bench did not name him. Notice was also issued on separate petitions by AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi and Congress leader Digvijaya Singh. No interim order was reported. The Hindustan Times had reported on 12 October that the batch of SIR petitions was listed for 27 October.
items.quote: "We would also ask one of the petitioners about his conduct."
items.response: No counsel for the Commission was reported. The Court said "Somebody will accept notice on behalf of the Election Commission of India," Bar and Bench reported.
items.note: Hearing Thursday 15 October 2026. LiveLaw 12:55 pm IST. Bar and Bench quotes the CJI: 'Issuing notice does not mean that we are condemning anything' and 'The notice on behalf of one of the petitioners will be entertained on a provisional basis.' The Tribune (3:23 pm) has the same. The Week (Kanu Sarda, 2:43 pm) headlines that the Court asked Rahul Gandhi to explain the march, but its text says the bench did not identify the petitioner, so naming him is the paper's inference and is left out. Bar and Bench's live updates put the SIR petitions at items 24, 25 and 45, returnable on a common date that is not given. The remarks 'Nobody can browbeat' and 'We are not sitting in ivory towers', which the Tribune and LawBeat place in this hearing, were made on a separate petition about the march (court-44), per LiveLaw 554802 and Bar and Bench's live updates. The Court's written order of 15 October was not found on sci.gov.in. The 27 October listing is from the Hindustan Times of 12 October 2026 (Utkarsh Anand), read in full on 24 October 2026; see court-49.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1360 of 2026 (Diary No. 64394 of 2026), a petition by four advocates on the march of 12 October, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'Nobody Can Browbeat Us' : Supreme Court In Plea Against October 12 March By Political Leaders; Issues Notice
items.claim: The same bench issued notice on a petition by four advocates about the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on 12 October, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for rules on demonstrations near the Supreme Court and the High Courts and for criminal contempt proceedings against Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav and Mahua Moitra. Senior counsel for the petitioners said about 200 lawyers had signed a memorandum calling the march browbeating. The Chief Justice said nobody could browbeat the Court and that the judges knew what was said outside it. The Court ordered CCTV footage of its premises, and footage held by law enforcement agencies, to be preserved. Bar and Bench reported that it declined to begin contempt proceedings that day.
items.quote: "Nobody can browbeat us," the CJI responded. ... "We are not sitting in ivory towers." "We know what statements they make outside and what they say in Court."
items.response: No reply from the leaders named was reported.
items.note: LiveLaw 1:13 pm IST, 15 October 2026. The petitioning advocates are private persons and are not named. Bar and Bench's live updates (item 30) record that the CJI declined to initiate contempt that day and issued notice only. The South First and DT Next report notice to the Congress, its Kerala unit and the four leaders, which LiveLaw does not state. The petition's contempt prayer is the petitioners' allegation.

items.outlet: Delhi High Court (order of 14.10.2026, as published by LiveLaw)
items.case: W.P.(C) 14955/2026, a petition by two electors, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi High Court closes a petition by two electors left off the roll and leaves them free to file Form 6
items.claim: The Delhi High Court closed a petition by two electors whose names were left off Delhi's roll after they moved house and could not fill the enumeration form. They had asked the Court to quash para 4(c) of the SIR guidelines, which sends such electors to Form 6 with the declaration, and to restore their entries and let them correct them through Form 8. The Commission's standing counsel said they could file Form 6 and that the Electoral Registration Officer would help. The first petitioner said that filing Form 6 would be a false declaration. The bench said that, since the suggestion came from the Commission's counsel on the officer's instructions, his fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced. It left them free to file Form 6, to be processed in accordance with law.
items.quote: Having heard learned counsel for the parties, we are of the considered opinion that when the suggestion is coming from the learned standing counsel appearing for ECI, that too as per the instructions of the Electoral Registration Officer, petitioner no.1’s apprehension that he would be accused of furnishing a false declaration is misplaced. ... With these observations, the writ proceedings are closed. Petitioners, if so desire, may fill Form 6, which shall be processed in accordance with law.
items.response: The Commission's standing counsel said the grievance could be redressed if the petitioners filed Form 6 under rule 25(2) read with rule 13(1)(a) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that he had asked the first petitioner to do so at the previous hearing and the Electoral Registration Officer would help.
items.note: Order of Justice Dinesh Mehta and Dr. Justice Aditi Choudhary, 14 October 2026, CNR DLHC010486872026, with CM APPL. 70130/2026 and 70131/2026; four pages, digitally signed, 'downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/10/2026', read in full from the copy LiveLaw links (PDF SHA-256 a2eb7da0...cd3147f). The Delhi High Court's own portal needs a captcha and was not used. LiveLaw report by Nupur Thapliyal, 16 October 2026, 2:49 pm IST, 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 1014, partly behind a subscription but its text was in the page. Prayer A asked to quash 'Paragraph 4(c) of Annexure B to Election Commission of India Order No. 23/ERS/2025 dated 24.06.2025, as made applicable to the NCT of Delhi vide ECI Letter No. 23/2025-ERS (Vol. II) dated 14.05.2026'. The order and LiveLaw say the names 'got deleted'; the petition says the electors could not be enumerated, so on the site's terms they were left off the draft. The order does not mention item (iii) of the Form 6 declaration, the words 'first time', or section 31 of the 1950 Act, does not decide prayer A, and does not say that signing item (iii) is lawful; it records the counsel's suggestion and calls the fear of being accused misplaced on that ground. The petitioners are private persons and are not named. Related: court-29 (Devender Yadav's petition on the first-time declaration, withdrawn on 10 September with leave to file a PIL). A separate Supreme Court petition on the same Form 6 question (LiveLaw 554528 and 554585, hearing advanced to 28 October 2026) was found and not added.

items.case: Plea on voter deletions in Maharashtra's SIR, Supreme Court (petitioner and case number not reported)
items.headline: Supreme Court Lists Maharashtra SIR Voter Deletions Plea For October 26, Says Matters Cannot Be Generalised
items.claim: The Supreme Court declined to issue notice on 15 October on a plea about deletions in Maharashtra's revision and listed it for 26 October, LawChakra reported. The Chief Justice refused to hear it with the other petitions on the revision and said the Court would take the states one at a time, Maharashtra first and then Delhi. The petition says about 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors were flagged for logical discrepancies, and the Commission had not yet replied. Bar and Bench reported that senior counsel for the petitioner, Arvind Datar, told the Court that 1.2 crore of Maharashtra's 9.79 crore electors had been flagged for logical discrepancies and that 40.6% of electors had been left off the roll in Pune and some other areas. He asked for notice to be issued that day so that the authorities could reply before 26 October, and the Chief Justice said "Not today. Not today."
items.quote: This cannot be generalised. We have to look at it state-wise.
items.response: LawChakra reported that the Election Commission's response was not yet on record. Maharashtra's period for claims and objections closes on 26 October, the day of the hearing.
items.note: LawChakra, published 15 October 2026, 1:51 pm IST, read with curl on 20 October 2026. Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi; senior advocate Arvind Datar for the petitioner, who is not named in the report. The 1.2 crore of 9.79 crore is the petition's figure. The site holds Maharashtra's roll before the revision as 9,78,54,049 (CEO's press note of 31 August 2026); the petition's 1.2 crore is close to the CEO's own count of electors with an anomaly or with no mapping, 1,22,24,007 (the release of 4 September 2026, data/maharashtra/raw/district_notices.csv), which covers both lists and not logical discrepancies alone. Bar and Bench, by Debayan Roy, published 15 October 2026, 12:11 pm IST (datePublished 2026-10-15T06:41:38Z, modified 16 October), read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026; it names Arvind Datar as senior counsel and gives the 40.6% figure for Pune and other areas, which is counsel's submission. The site has no Pune figure to set against it. The closing date of 26 October is the process page's Maharashtra entry 'Release of 12.10.2026: claims to 26.10.2026'.

items.case: Appeals by the Election Commission before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals
items.headline: Election Commission Seeks to Remove Half the Bengal Voters Judges Have Cleared For Inclusion
items.claim: The Election Commission had filed appeals before West Bengal's SIR appellate tribunals against the inclusion of at least 14,75,887 voters by 17 October, 49.2% of the 30,00,545 voters in the records whom judicial officers had examined and found eligible, The Wire reported from appeal records collected by the Civic Research Group. Malda, Murshidabad and Uttar Dinajpur hold 44.6% of these appeals. In the 41 seats where minorities are more than half the population the appeals equal 5.9% of the draft roll, and in the 89 seats where they are under 10% they equal 0.6%. The tribunals had decided 80,091 appeals, or 5.4%, and the report says no tribunal has been able to upload an order since 21 September. In a follow-up on 24 October, The Wire reported that the Civic Research Group's fuller records show 16,08,175 appeals by the Commission against 32,53,401 voters found eligible, 49.4%, close to the 16,10,311 the Commission reported to the Supreme Court. It reported that the appeal numbers carry a filing date, a structure that activists found and The Wire says it verified, and that 99.3% of the appeals in the records of 17 October carry one of three dates, 5, 6 or 8 April 2026, with more than 12 lakh on 5 April. The roll was frozen for the Assembly election at midnight on 7 April.
items.quote: The Commission has not disclosed on what grounds it is challenging these voters, and who exactly decided to file the appeals.
items.response: The report says the Commission has not said on what grounds it filed the appeals, who decided to file them, or whether each case was reviewed before an appeal was filed. The follow-up says only the Commission can confirm the dates read from the appeal numbers, and that a single date on more than 12 lakh appeals does not by itself show who authorised them.
items.note: The Wire, went live 21 October 2026, 7:23 pm (article:published_date 2026-10-21T13:53:24+05:30), read in full on 22 October 2026 via Firecrawl. No byline on the page. The records are the Civic Research Group's (appeal.civicresearch.in), which the report calls an independent group of researchers in West Bengal. Figures as of 17 October. The site does not hold appeal records and cannot check these counts. The report's wording is 'remove'; here the appeals are against inclusion. Follow-up by Aparna Bhattacharya, published 24 October 2026, 11:00 am IST (post_date_gmt 05:30:56), read in full through The Wire's CMS API (posts/detail) on 24 October 2026. The dates come from the activists' reading of the ID series letters, which the report says Election Commission sources confirmed; the three dates cover 13,85,374 of 13,95,794 appeal IDs. Its ID analysis uses the extract of 17 October with 14,75,885 appeals, two fewer than the 14,75,887 in the first report. The site's West Bengal summary has 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion of 32,68,119 found eligible, 49.27%.

items.case: Application by two transparency activists in their pending petition on the Delhi SIR, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026, Supreme Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court Advances Hearing After Plea Flags Deleted Voters Being Asked To Fill Form 6
items.claim: Two transparency activists who had petitioned the Court on the Delhi revision filed an application against the requirement that electors left off Delhi's draft apply again on Form 6, whose declaration says the applicant is applying for inclusion for the first time, LiveLaw reported. The application says 47,56,722 electors, 32.78% of those on the roll before the revision, were left off the draft, and that a false declaration can be punished under section 31 of the 1950 Act. It asks for a way to restore these electors without that declaration, and for the additional declaration form added to Forms 6 and 8 through the SIR guidelines to be declared without statutory authority because it was not made under section 28 of the Act. Counsel asked the Court to let them use Form 8 or another form. On 14 October the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi moved the hearing of the main petition from 30 to 28 October.
items.quote: we are thinking of passing an order that will take care of [all this]
items.response: No submission by the Commission was reported. Counsel told the Court that 30 October was the last date in Delhi for correcting deletions.
items.note: Hearing of 14 October: LiveLaw, by Debby Jain and Amisha Shrivastava, published 14 October 2026, 11:55 am IST. The application: LiveLaw, by Gursimran Kaur Bakshi, published 13 October 2026, 11:10 pm IST, which gives the case as Anjali Bhardwaj & Anr v. Election Commission of India & Anr, W.P.(C) No. 1188 of 2026. Both read in full on 24 October 2026 with curl, from the JSON-LD articleBody and, where that is cut short, the page text. The quote is the Chief Justice's, as LiveLaw prints it. Counsel was Prashant Bhushan. The activists are given by role, as in court-30, which is the main petition. The application's 47,56,722 and 32.78% equal the site's own Delhi figures (removed 4,756,722 of 14,510,299, 32.78 per 100, in data/india/states.json), from the CEO's press note of 31 August 2026. Related: court-29 and court-45 on the same Form 6 declaration.

items.case: A fresh writ petition on the modified Form 6, Supreme Court (petitioner not reported)
items.headline: We have neither approved nor disapproved ECI's Form 6 modification: Supreme Court clarifies
items.claim: On a fresh writ petition, the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said its remarks of 5 October meant only that the modified Form 6 did not exist when the Bihar case was heard, and that the Court had neither approved nor disapproved it, Bar and Bench reported. Counsel for the petitioner had said the Commission was presenting the altered form as approved by the Court. The Hindustan Times reported that the bench said it would examine the issue and listed the petition with the batch of SIR petitions on 27 October, when it would also take up the wider challenge to how the Commission's decisions on the revision were taken.
items.quote: What was said was that when the Bihar SIR matter was before us, the new Form 6 was not there. That does not mean it was either approved or disapproved by the Supreme Court
items.response: The Commission's press note of 26 September said the Supreme Court had upheld the additional declaration attached to Form 6 for the revision. The Hindustan Times reported that the Commission maintains the statutory form itself was not altered and that the declaration is an addendum for the revision only.
items.note: Bar and Bench, by Debayan Roy, published 12 October 2026, 1:10 pm IST (modified 13 October). Hindustan Times, by Utkarsh Anand, published 12 October 2026, 2:48 pm IST. Both read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The quote is Justice Bagchi's, as Bar and Bench prints it. Neither report names the petitioner. The remark of 5 October is court-31. The 27 October listing is the only next date for the batch read so far; see court-43.

items.case: PIL by an advocate for an expert committee on the Election Commission, Supreme Court
items.headline: Plea before Supreme Court seeks expert committee headed by former CJI to examine ECI's functioning
items.claim: An advocate filed a PIL in the Supreme Court asking for an independent expert committee, chaired by a former Chief Justice or judge of the Court, to examine shortcomings in the functioning of the Election Commission, Bar and Bench reported. It relies on The Indian Express report of 23 September that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi recorded written objections at least 14 times over ten months to decisions taken by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar alone. Citing reports of a Commission affidavit, it says about 38.20 lakh appeals had been filed in West Bengal by people excluded from the roll and about 1.02 lakh decided. It also asks the Commission to bar campaigning on religious tags, religious symbols and communal appeals. No hearing date was reported.
items.quote: The petition states that it is intended to be non-partisan and prospective and that the petitioner is not seeking a finding against any political party or office-holder, nor does it challenge the result of any election.
items.response: The plea says the Commission acknowledged the dissenting notes and described them as routine suggestions. The plea describes all the West Bengal appeals as filed by people excluded from the roll. The Commission's own count splits them into 22,21,118 appeals by people found not eligible and 16,10,311 appeals against inclusion.
items.note: Bar and Bench, by Debayan Roy, published 24 October 2026, 9:57 am IST, read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The quote is Bar and Bench's summary of the petition. The petitioner is an advocate and a private person, and is not named. The site's West Bengal summary (data/westbengal/summary.json) has 38,31,429 appeals, 22,21,118 by the excluded and 16,10,311 against inclusion, so the plea's 38.20 lakh is close to the total and its description of who filed them differs from the Commission's split. The report also says the plea cites a Maharashtra birth-year error that showed 2,70,313 electors aged 101 to 150 on the draft. That figure's official source was not read and it is left out of the claim. The dissent notes are the subject of court-31.
